text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong hits out at opposition politician Chee Soon Juan for not defending Singapore.
- Breakaway Khmer Rouge commanders agree to merge their 4,000 fighters with Cambodian government forces.
- Property developers and agents account for 97 percent of real estate industry operating profit of Singapore $5.5 billion in 1994.
- British Telecommunications says it will acquire MCI Communications Corp in cash-and-stock transaction worth about U.S. $20 billion.
- U.S. polls could set tone for Wall Street.
- Creative Technology announces return to profitability with U.S. $14.7 million first-quarter net profit after two quarters in the red.

- Singapore Technologies Telemedia, the telecommunications arm of the government-linked conglomerate, is prepared to invest up to Singapore $2 billion in key telecoms projects in Singapore and the region.
- U.S. analysts warns that Wall Street and its bond counterpart could dive if foreign central banks decide to take profits on U.S. Treasury bonds.
- Hongkong-listed electronics company Integrated Display Technology International plans to list liquid crystal display business on SES mainboard.
- Ho Wah Genting International says attempt by majority shareholders to sell 41.1 percent stake in company was called off.
